# COBIT and ISO 31000 citation existence

A cited governance-framework code resolves to a real entry in its reference
catalogue. The check reads each document outside fenced code blocks and flags four
citation defects: a token matching the COBIT objective-code shape (a domain prefix
and objective number, with an optional practice suffix) that is not a catalogued
objective; a real objective cited with a practice number outside the inclusive valid
range the catalogue records for it; the wrong ISO 31000 designation (`ISO/IEC 31000`
rather than `ISO 31000`); and an ISO 31000 clause number that is not in the standard's
clause set. The code-shape and designation regexes, the clause-token parser (including
its table-cell adjacency logic), and the four defect tests are fixed in the check
implementation; the reference catalogue (the objective codes and titles, the
per-objective practice counts, and the ISO 31000 clause set) and the scan scope and
exempt-file set are project configuration. A code that resolves cleanly, a citation
inside a fenced code block, and a document that cites none contribute no finding.
